1#main: Several laws of sending away the mother bird. In it are 13 seifim. Sending away the mother bird applies only to a pure bird—even if the mother is a treifah; and even if there is only one fledgling or one egg, he is obligated to send her away.
2#main: A nest that is ready at hand, such as doves that are accustomed to be raised with people in houses, and geese and chickens that nested in a house—is exempt. But doves of a dovecote and an attic, and birds that nested in earthenware vessels (meaning: clay vessels built in walls where birds nest), and in pits—and geese and chickens that nested in an orchard—are obligated; and this is when the mother was not raised above the eggs at all from when she laid them. But if the mother was raised above them, if those places are his, his courtyard acquired it for him and it is ready at hand and exempt.
3#main: And wherever one finds it—whether in a tree, whether on the ground, or in pits, channels, and caves, or in the sea, or on a person's head, or on the head of another domestic animal—whether in the public domain or in private domain, he is obligated to send her away.
4#main: He must send the mother until she leaves from under his hand; and afterward he takes the young. And if he wishes to cut her wings before sending her so she cannot fly, and then take her—he may not; rather he sends her immediately with her wings so she can fly. And after she leaves his hand he may take her if he wishes. And if he cut them, he waits until her wings grow and sends her.
5#main: If he wishes to take the mother and send the young—he may not. He sends her, and she returns—he sends her and she returns, even many times, he must return and send her. But if he sent her and took the young and returned them to the nest and the mother returned upon them, he is exempt from sending.
6#main: If he took the mother from upon the young and did not send her—he sends her and is exempt.
7#main: If the eggs were spoiled or the fledglings were flying, or they are treifah; or a male is lying on the nest; or an impure bird on the eggs of a pure bird, or a pure bird on the eggs of an impure bird—he is exempt from sending (words of the Rambam, chapter 13 of Hilchos Shechitah, halachah 10).
8#main: If she was lying on eggs that are not her species and they are pure—he sends away; and if he did not send, he does not receive lashes (there, halachah 11).
9#main: If it was a cloth or wings of another bird, or spoiled eggs—they interrupt between her and the nest; or if there were two rows of eggs one on the other and her wings touch the upper row; or if one mother was upon another; or if the male was on the nest and the mother on the male—he sends away; and if he did not send, he does not receive lashes (there, halachah 14).
10#main: If he slaughtered part of the simanim of the fledglings in the nest before taking them—he sends away; and if he did not send, he does not receive lashes (there, halachah 12).
11#main: If she was fluttering over the nest—if her wings touch the nest, he is obligated to send; and if not, he is exempt, even though they touch from the side.
12#main: If she was sitting between the eggs or between the fledglings—even if she touches them, she is exempt.
13#main: If she was sitting on two branches of the tree and the nest is beneath her—if it appears that were she to slip she would fall upon them, he is obligated; and if not, he is exempt.
